name: flag-justify
description: One gate flag (content-diff or visual-diff line) at a prototype or published gate: an artefact or an intended, documented difference — or a defect to fix? (#126)

fields.flag: { probe: 'content'|'visual'|'chrome', line: the finding as printed, severity }
fields.gate: { page, width, regime: 'prototype'|'published', summary: the probe's header lines (node counts per side) }
fields.policy: the run's capture-state and register policy in a few lines (what is known to vary between loads, what the inconsistency register permits)

instructions.question: Is `flag` an artefact of how the pages were captured or compared, rather than a difference a reader of the build would see?
instructions.focus: Artefacts: a heuristic false positive (object-fit images read as stretched, lazy images below the fold not yet loaded when sampled), machine-only text (JSON-LD or script bodies counted as body copy), the same words split or joined across elements, a count that differs by whitespace.

criteria.true: A reader comparing the two pages would see no difference; the instrument or its heuristic reports one.
criteria.false: A reader would see the difference the flag names.

instructions.question: Does `policy` cover the difference `flag` names as an intended, documented one — content that varies between loads of the origin (a carousel slide, a rotating offer, personalised text, a date) frozen at its captured state, or a change the inconsistency register permits?
instructions.focus: Only what `policy` names counts; do not assume a policy that is not stated.

criteria.true: The policy names this kind of variation or this permitted change.
criteria.false: The policy does not cover it, or names nothing of the kind.

instructions.question: Would a reader of the build miss or misread content because of `flag` — a heading, body text, a link or an image that is present on the origin and absent, hidden or reworded on the build?
instructions.focus: Judge the visible outcome, not the instrument's severity mark.

criteria.true: Content a reader would use is missing, hidden or changed in meaning on the build.
criteria.false: Nothing a reader would use is missing or changed; the difference is cosmetic, machine-only, or a re-wrapping of the same words.
